body:
Come to think of it, is makes sense that it's happening (infinite recursion), but it feels like a weird spot for this API. I incorrectly assumed parallels from Unity:
* That EditorInspectorPlugin allowed to customize how the inspector presents an object, like a CustomEditor in Unity. It does that in a way, but its main purpose is to "add custom **property editors** on the inspector" ([doc](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_editorinspectorplugin.html)), which is not exactly the same.
* That `EditorInspector.instantiate_property_editor()` allowed to instantiate the "default" EditorProperty for a given property on my object, with the actual node hierarchy and logic for applying value changes on my object, etc. (like a PropertyField in Unity). It does, but I assume it goes through EditorInspector, but also every EditorInspectorPlugin in the project to see **how** I want this property edited (thank you very much). It should then never be used in EditorInspectorPlugin, and is only useful in custom UI windows.

Because afaik the actual default EditorProperty are not exposed, it feels a bit limiting. I guess this is not a bug, but still, probably something that could be clarified in the documentation (and result in a compile error ?). 

Ultimately, it feels like the functions of how the inspector presents a given object and how it presents a given property shouldn't be tightly coupled like this.

I don't know if the code you wrote is your exact use case. The main issue is just passing the exact same parameters to instantiate property editor. As well as not having any filters. I've done a property selector. Which just instantiated an enum editor if the hint_string was "propertylist". Otherwise I couldn't get dynamic list by just exporting an enum.
It looks like you intention may have been just to double every inspector property?

_parse_begin and _parse_end are probably more similar to what you expected. Your other option is also just returning false. It won't delete any of the controls you added and can just pass through (I'm pretty sure at least)

I'm going for a more compact and manageable inspector, which is proving a bit painful with what Godot provides but is also a fun way to understand the inner workings. In source, I saw that `EditorInspectorDefaultPlugin::get_editor_for_property()` is what I expected `instantiate_property_editor` to be, however `EditorInspectorDefaultPlugin` is not exposed, and while this gives the correct `Control` for the property type, I'm not entirely sure it hooks up all the relevant inspector behaviors and signals. > The main issue is just passing the exact same parameters to instantiate property editor. You're right, I could probably manipulate hint type/hint string/usage flags by adding a custom value, and then return false if I detect this when it's parsed next. It would stop the recursion and give me the `EditorProperty`. For now, I've resolved to just visit the tree in `_parse_end()` and do what I need to there, which is heavier but it doesn't really matter for the inspector. It's also useful to change some other "sensible defaults" that I dislike. However it's something that is bound to break with updates, and also requires to handle every edge case, so having a robust custom inspector workflow from the API would be cool! | Base| Custom | |--------|--------| | | |
